# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

I see a display reading 0, a yellow light, and three wires in order: red, yellow, blue. I’m telling both teammates the complete visible state so the Mute can apply the manual and the Blind can identify and manipulate the correct parts. The incoming gestures do not convey usable meaning to me without a prearranged code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb state: display reads 0. Light is yellow. Wires from left to right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please use the manual and tell Blind what to do.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display reads zero. The light is yellow. Wires from left to right are wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Await the Mute's manual instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display 0, yellow light, and wires red, yellow, blue from left to right. I can see the Mute’s two-finger gesture, but no meaning has been established for it, so I should not infer an instruction from it. I will restate the state and direct the Blind to follow the Mute’s manual-based instructions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see your two-finger gesture, but its meaning is not established. The visible state remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please give Blind the exact manual instruction by speech.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Follow the Mute's exact manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The visible bomb state is still unchanged: display 0, yellow light, and wires red, yellow, blue in positions 1–3. The repeated ✌ gesture may be intentional, but without an agreed code I cannot safely interpret it. The Mute should communicate the manual’s exact instruction verbally to the Blind, who can then act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind; I cannot safely interpret the repeated two-finger gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please listen for and follow the Mute's exact manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. The Mute’s latest gesture is 🫵 ✌, which most naturally means “you, two”: an instruction directed to the Blind concerning item 2. Given that the Mute has the manual and the Blind is the only one who can act, I will relay that the intended action appears to involve wire 2, while identifying the gesture as the source rather than claiming certainty beyond it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured 🫵 ✌, apparently directing you to wire 2. The bomb still shows display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The intended manual action appears to concern wire 2.")
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret your latest gesture 🫵 ✌ as directing Blind to wire 2. Blind has been told this, along with the unchanged bomb state.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that wire 2 was the correct wire and was cut successfully. The bomb has changed: display remains 0, the light is now blue, and wire 2 is cut; wires 1 and 3 remain red and blue. I will report this new state so the Mute can apply the next manual step and the Blind knows the successful action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: wire 2 was correct and is cut. The bomb changed. Current state: display 0, light blue, wire 1 red, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue. Please determine and state the next manual instruction for Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: your cut of wire 2 was correct. Current state: display 0, light blue, wire 1 red, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue. Await the Mute's next manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged after the successful cut of wire 2: display 0, blue light, wire 1 red, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue. The Mute now gestures 🫵 🤟, which follows the established pattern of directing the Blind to a wire number; 🤟 appears to indicate wire 3. I will relay that instruction to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured 🫵 🤟, directing you to wire 3. Current state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 red, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue. Please perform the manual's indicated action on wire 3.")
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret 🫵 🤟 as directing Blind to wire 3. I relayed that instruction. Current display 0, blue light; wire 2 is cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤟]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that wire 3 was also correct and is now cut. The bomb has changed again: display 0, red light, wire 1 red, and wires 2 and 3 cut. The repeated gesture likely referred to the successful wire-3 action already taken, so I will report the new state and avoid directing Blind to cut an already-cut wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: wire 3 was correct and is now cut. Current state: display 0, red light, wire 1 red, wire 2 cut, wire 3 cut. Please determine the next manual instruction.")
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: wire 3 was correct and is now cut. Current state: display 0, red light, wire 1 red, wire 2 cut, wire 3 cut. Do not repeat a cut; await the Mute's next manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ☝]

The bomb is unchanged: display 0, red light, wire 1 red, and wires 2 and 3 cut. The established gesture-number code makes 🫵 ☝ indicate wire 1. Since it is the only remaining uncut wire, I will tell the Blind to cut wire 1.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured 🫵 ☝, directing you to wire 1. Current state: display 0, red light, wire 1 red, wires 2 and 3 cut. Cut wire 1.")
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret 🫵 ☝ as directing Blind to cut wire 1, and I relayed that instruction. Current state: display 0, red light; wires 2 and 3 are cut.")
wait()
```
